paragraphs.title: Solomon's Appointment and the Census of the Levites

easy.explanation: David made Solomon his son king over Israel.
easy.q: Whom did David make king over Israel?

easy.explanation: David gathered the priests and the Levites with the princes.
easy.q: Whom did David gather with the princes of Israel?

easy.explanation: Their number was thirty and eight thousand.
easy.q: How many Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward?

medium.explanation: Twenty and four thousand were appointed for the work of the house of the LORD.
medium.q: How many Levites were appointed to set forward the work of the house of the LORD?

medium.explanation: Six thousand were officers and judges.
medium.q: What role did six thousand Levites have?

answers: By the names of their cities
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the Levites were counted individually.
medium.q: What does “by their polls, man by man” mean?

challenge.explanation: The passage names officers, judges, porters, and those who praised the LORD.
challenge.q: Which combination of duties appears in the census of the Levites?

challenge.explanation: There were four thousand porters and four thousand who praised the LORD.
challenge.q: How many Levites were assigned to be porters and singers together?

answers: They were divided into different roles
They all served only as singers
They all served only as judges
challenge.explanation: The Levites served in administration, judgment, guarding, and praise.
challenge.q: What does the variety of duties show about the Levites?

paragraphs.title: The Division of the Levitical Families

easy.explanation: David divided the Levites among Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
easy.q: Into which three groups did David divide the sons of Levi?

easy.explanation: The sons of Laadan were Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
easy.q: Who were listed as the sons of Laadan?

easy.explanation: The passage names three sons of Laadan.
easy.q: How many sons of Laadan are named?

medium.explanation: Jehiel was the chief, followed by Zetham and Joel.
medium.q: Who was the chief of the sons of Laadan?

medium.explanation: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran are listed as three.
medium.q: How many sons of Shimei are listed in the first mention?

answers: They were counted as one father’s house
medium.explanation: Because they did not have many sons, they were counted together as one father’s house.
medium.q: What does “according to their father's house” indicate about Jeush and Beriah?

challenge.explanation: The passage first lists three and later lists four sons of Shimei.
challenge.q: What difference appears in the numbers of Shimei's sons in the passage?

challenge.explanation: Jehiel is called the chief of the sons of Laadan.
challenge.q: Which name is identified as a chief before other names are listed?

answers: Their number affected how their household was counted
challenge.explanation: Their small number led them to be counted together as one father’s house.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the statement that Jeush and Beriah “had not many sons”?

paragraphs.title: The Kohathite Families and the Priestly Distinction

easy.explanation: The four sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
easy.q: Who were the four sons of Kohath?

easy.explanation: Aaron was separated for the special holy service.
easy.q: Who was separated to sanctify the most holy things?

easy.explanation: Moses' sons were named of the tribe of Levi.
easy.q: Of which tribe were Moses' sons named?

answers: To burn incense, minister, and bless in God's name
medium.explanation: They were appointed to burn incense, minister unto the LORD, and bless in his name.
medium.q: What was Aaron and his sons' work according to the passage?

medium.explanation: Shebuel was the chief of the sons of Gershom.
medium.q: Who was the chief of the sons of Gershom?

answers: Set apart for a special duty
medium.explanation: Aaron was set apart for the special priestly service.
medium.q: What does “separated” mean in the description of Aaron?

answers: Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses
Moses was the father of Aaron and Amram
Aaron was the father of Moses and Amram
challenge.explanation: Aaron and Moses are listed as the sons of Amram.
challenge.q: What important family relationship is described?

answers: Aaron's sons were set apart for priestly service, while Moses' sons were Levites
Moses' sons were priests, while Aaron was only a Levite
challenge.explanation: Aaron was separated with his sons for holy service, while Moses' sons were identified with Levi.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between Aaron's sons and Moses' sons?

answers: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, Jekameam; Micah and Jesiah
Micah, Jahaziel, Jeriah, Amariah; Jekameam and Jesiah
Shebuel, Rehabiah, Shelomith; Micah and Jesiah
challenge.explanation: The sons of Hebron are listed in that order, followed by the sons of Uzziel.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly lists the chiefs and descendants in the passage?

easy.explanation: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi.
easy.q: Who were the two sons of Merari?

easy.explanation: The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
easy.q: Who were the sons of Mahli?

easy.explanation: Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
easy.q: How many sons of Mushi are named?

answers: They were taken by the sons of Kish
They were counted among Mushi's sons
medium.explanation: The sons of Kish took Eleazar's daughters.
medium.q: What happened to Eleazar's daughters after his death?

answers: He had daughters but no sons
medium.explanation: The passage says that Eleazar had no sons, but daughters.
medium.q: Why were no sons counted for Eleazar?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to counting the Levites according to their family lines.
medium.q: What does “after the house of their fathers” refer to?

answers: A marriage connection between two families
challenge.explanation: The passage describes a family connection between Eleazar's daughters and Kish's sons.
challenge.q: What family connection resulted from the sons of Kish taking Eleazar's daughters?

answers: Merari: Mahli and Mushi; Mahli: Eleazar and Kish; Mushi: three sons
Merari: Aaron and Moses; Mahli: Gershom; Mushi: Kohath
Merari: Jehiel and Zetham; Mahli: Beriah; Mushi: Shelomith
challenge.explanation: This sequence follows the family relationships listed in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the families of Merari?

challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly concludes by saying that there were three.
challenge.q: What detail might be missed when reading the list of Mushi's sons quickly?

paragraphs.title: The Transition to Temple Service in Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward.
easy.q: From what age were the Levites counted for the service of the house of the LORD?

easy.explanation: David said that Israel would dwell in Jerusalem for ever.
easy.q: Where did the LORD give Israel rest to dwell?

easy.explanation: They would no more carry the Tabernacle or any of its vessels.
easy.q: What were the Levites no longer required to carry?

answers: They no longer carried the Tabernacle
medium.explanation: The change was connected with the Levites no longer carrying the Tabernacle.
medium.q: Why was the census extended to Levites twenty years old and above?

medium.explanation: They served in the courts, chambers, and the purification of holy things.
medium.q: Where did the Levites wait on the sons of Aaron?

medium.explanation: Their office was their appointed responsibility in the house of the LORD.
medium.q: What does the phrase “their office” refer to?

answers: From carrying the Tabernacle to serving in a permanent sanctuary
From guarding to going to war
challenge.explanation: The Levites no longer carried the Tabernacle but served in the house of the LORD.
challenge.q: What was the main change in the Levites' work?

answers: Assisting the priests, guarding, and purifying holy things
Crowning kings, writing books, and fighting wars
Building cities, collecting taxes, and judging the people
challenge.explanation: Their duties included assisting Aaron's sons, guarding, and purifying holy things.
challenge.q: Which combination best describes the Levites' service?

answers: A settled place allowed service without carrying the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The settled dwelling place made it possible for the Levites to serve without transporting the Tabernacle.
challenge.q: How are Israel's rest in Jerusalem and the Levites' changed work related?

easy.explanation: They stood every morning and likewise at even.
easy.q: When did the Levites stand to thank and praise the LORD?

answers: Sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts
At the beginning of the year only
easy.explanation: The passage names the sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts.
easy.q: On which occasions did the Levites offer the burnt sacrifices?

answers: The Tabernacle, the holy place, and the sons of Aaron
easy.explanation: They kept charge of the Tabernacle, the holy place, and the sons of Aaron.
easy.q: What did the Levites keep charge of?

medium.explanation: Their work included the shewbread and fine flour for meat offerings.
medium.q: Which items did the Levites prepare?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to measuring and handling the required quantities.
medium.q: What duty is connected with “all manner of measure and size”?

medium.explanation: To keep charge meant to carry out an assigned responsibility.
medium.q: What does “charge” mean in this passage?

answers: Preparing offerings, measuring, praising, serving on feast days, and guarding
Preparing bread and offering sacrifices only
challenge.explanation: The passage lists many different duties performed by the Levites.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the variety of the Levites' work?

answers: Praise was part of a regular continuing order
Praise happened only on rare occasions
challenge.explanation: The morning and evening schedule shows that praise was regular and continual.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the repeated mention of morning and evening praise?

challenge.explanation: They kept charge of the sons of Aaron their brethren.
challenge.q: For whom did the Levites keep charge in addition to the holy place?
